answer: In a crowdsourced terrain-mapping task, each annotation becomes a vertex in a similarity graph. A vertex too similar to an existing one joins its cluster, and the cluster's entire payout goes to its earliest member; later members earn nothing. Fifty sybil copies of an honest mapper's dune outline therefore take none of her reward. The first outline of an unmapped canyon is paid in full, so sybils profit only from genuinely new work.
